stance_line: Cautious. I want to see it run on something before I believe it.
message:
I'd like a tool that tells me which links in my notes folder go nowhere. I run it once after a tidy-up.

How my notes look: headings use hash signs. Links are plain, like "see Shoes" or "see First Call". After my tidy-up, notes are in folders and some have new names. Please look at how links can be written in markdown, and tell me in plain words which forms you check. If my "see Shoes" style is something you can't be sure of, ask me. Don't guess.

Limits:
- One file I can read top to bottom, plus its tests. No manual and no options beyond the folder name.
- It must never change, move or delete my notes. It only reads and prints.
- Right both ways matters more than clever. A missed dead link is no use. A good link called broken is worse, because I'll stop believing it.
- If two notes could match one link, say so. Don't quietly pick one.
- Show me the output of a run on your test folder. I'll judge by that.

I'll add these requirements now.

New requirements, build them together:
- I run it with one thing, the folder name. For each dead link it prints the file, the line number, and what the link was pointing at. It exits with an error status if there are any. If there are none it prints one plain line saying so. (I will check: Run it on the test folder with known dead links and see file:line and target for each one. Run it on a clean folder and see the single 'no dead links' line and a zero exit.)
- A link to a note in another folder, or to a note that was renamed and linked under the new name, is not reported when the note exists. It looks through the whole folder tree, not just the same folder. (I will check: In the test folder, a note in a nested subfolder is linked from a note in the top folder and from a note in a different subfolder. Neither link appears in the output.)
- A link to a heading inside a note is checked against the hash-sign headings actually in that note. A heading that is there is not reported. A heading that isn't there is reported. (I will check: The test folder has one link to a heading that exists and one to a heading that doesn't. Only the second is printed.)
- A link to a note that doesn't exist yet, like my Rings note pointing at a family note I haven't written, is reported every run, in the same words each time. There is no way to silence it. (I will check: The test folder has a note linking to a missing note. It appears in the output on two runs in a row, identical.)
- If a link could match more than one note (same name in two folders), the tool says that plainly, naming both files, instead of choosing one and calling the link good or broken. (I will check: The test folder has two notes with the same name in different folders and a link to that name. The output names both files for that link.)

message:
Thanks, the output is what I wanted: file, line, what it pointed at, and the same words on the second run.

Two things.

1. The name. The check I've been given looks for a file called linkcheck.py, and you've called yours deadlinks.py. Please rename it to linkcheck.py and the tests to test_linkcheck.py. Keep it one file plus tests, and make sure the check passes with that name. I don't want to type a name that differs from what's written down.

2. "see Shoes". Don't guess at plain prose. "see you Tuesday" flagged as dead would finish my trust in it. But I don't want it quietly ignored either, because a miss is as bad as a false alarm. So leave plain "see ..." unchecked, and at the end print one line saying how many lines have "see " in plain words and weren't checked. Then I'll know what it didn't look at. If the count is big, I'll tell you what my real links look like.

Questions, since you assumed them:
- Why are upper and lower case the same? If I have "Shoes" and "shoes" as two notes, does it call that ambiguous, or does it pick one?
- If a link has a folder in it, like old/Shoes.md, and Shoes has since moved to a different folder, do you report it dead? I think that's right, but tell me what it does.

Limits: it reads only, it's one file, and it needs no settings and no manual. I should be able to read all of it. Also make sure no dead link is dropped if the same link appears twice on a line.

New requirements, build them together:
- At the end of a run, if any lines contain a plain-words 'see ...' that isn't a proper link, it prints one line saying how many such lines were not checked. Those lines are never reported as dead. (I will check: Put 'see Shoes' and 'see you Tuesday' in plain text in a test note; run it; neither is reported as dead, and the closing line says 2 lines were not checked.)
- The tool is one file called linkcheck.py, with its tests in test_linkcheck.py, and I run it as python3 linkcheck.py FOLDER. (I will check: ls shows linkcheck.py and test_linkcheck.py and no deadlinks.py; python3 linkcheck.py test_notes prints the same dead links as before.)

ideas.text: At the end of every run, one line saying how many notes it read and how many links it checked, before the dead count. Like a test runner saying 212 passed, 3 failed. When it says no dead links, I want to see it actually looked at something, not an empty folder or a wrong folder name.
ideas.test: Run it on my real folder: the line shows roughly 300 notes, which I can compare with the count Finder gives me. Run it on an empty folder or a mistyped name and it says so plainly (0 notes read) and exits with an error, rather than saying all is well.
ideas.came_from: I stopped believing the insurer's letters, and the run that came back with file names not what I was told (day 43). A clean report is only worth something if I can see what it covered.

ideas.text: When a dead link is close to the name of a note that does exist, add a hint on that same report line, like git's 'did you mean'. Example: 'Notes/Rings.md line 4: see Shoe, dead. Did you mean Shoes.md?'. It still counts as dead. The hint is only a hint and never changes what is reported. No hint if nothing is close, so the Rings-to-family link stays plain and the same every run.
ideas.test: In the test folder, make a note that links to 'Shoe' while only Shoes.md exists. The line is reported dead and names Shoes.md. A link to 'Family' with nothing similar shows no hint. The dead count is the same with or without hints.
ideas.came_from: The tidy-up last month where I renamed and merged things and now can't tell if a click fails because of the note or because of me. Most of my dead links will be a renamed note, and I'd like to be pointed at it.

ideas.text: After the dead links and the 'see' count, one more line: how many notes no other note links to. Print their names only if there are ten or fewer, otherwise just the number. Nothing is changed or moved.
ideas.test: In the test folder, one note that nobody links to shows up by name. Link to it from another note, run again, and it drops off. Run on my real folder and I recognise at least one name, so I know it's right.
ideas.came_from: Marta asking me to train Kieran and the folder being all I have to give him. A note nothing leads to is one he would never find, and I'd want to know about it before I print them for Nula at Devonport.

stance_line: Seven tests passing isn't the same as me seeing it right. Show me the output.
message:
Don't guess at my folder, you're right about that. Stay in your test folders.

I can't tell you the exact brackets. I typed my links as "see Shoes", "see First Call" and "see Rings". Some may have the brackets round them and I don't remember which. So I need to know what your tool does with each of these:
1. `see Shoes` with nothing around it
2. `[see Shoes](Shoes.md)`
3. `[see Shoes](../Practical/Shoes.md)`
4. `[First Call](First Call.md#Rings)`, with a space in the name

Please put one of each in a test folder, some good and some dead. Then paste me the real output of a run, word for word, and the exit status. Don't summarise it. Then tell me which of the four it counts as checked links and which it only counts under "see".

If a good link is on the dead list, that is the worst outcome for me. So tell me the cases where you think it might wrongly report one. Names with spaces and capital letters are the ones I'd worry about.

Limits: it stays one file I can read, and there are no options or config to learn. The seven tests were enough to pass, but I want to know what they cover. Name them in a line each.

message:
Thank you, that I can read. The three dead ones look right.

You showed me dead links. You didn't show me a good link that stayed quiet. Please run it again on the same folder and print the good links too, so I can see them go by as fine. I want to be sure it isn't only saying dead things.

Then the two cases you skipped. Put them in the demo folder and show me the real output:
1. Two notes with the same name in different folders, and a link to that name. It should name both files.
2. A Rings note pointing at a family note that doesn't exist. It should come up dead, and the wording should be the same on a second run.

You said a heading with a link inside it "may not match". I don't want "may". Please fix it, or tell me plainly it can't be done. I've added it as a requirement.

Limits: still one file and its tests, and read-only. Keep the code short enough that I can read it, and no options. Don't add anything I haven't asked for.

For the 2 "see ..." lines: I click mine and get nothing, so I think mine are bracketed. Print the file and line of each unchecked one, so I can check for myself. I won't call that done yet. I'd like to see it first.

New requirements, build them together:
- A link to a heading whose title has other marks in it (a link, bold, or trailing hash signs) is matched on the plain words of the heading. If the words are there, it is not reported. (I will check: A demo note with a heading like '## See [Shoes](Shoes.md)' or '## Rings ##' and a link to it. Run it. The link is not reported. A link to a wrong heading in the same note still is.)
